title: Why UK Doctors Struggle to Give Patients Enough Time
subtitle: New research shows that most family doctors are too busy to discuss long-term health habits with their patients.

summary.en: A new study shows that three out of four family doctors in the UK feel they lack the time to talk to patients in depth. Doctors are currently overwhelmed by a high number of patients and urgent health problems. This makes it difficult for them to provide advice on lifestyle changes like quitting smoking or losing weight. Experts warn that this prevents the healthcare system from focusing on stopping illnesses before they start. The Royal College of GPs argues that the government must hire more doctors to fix this issue.
summary.zh: 一項新研究顯示，英國有四分之三的家庭醫師認為自己缺乏時間與病患進行深入交談。醫師目前因病患數量龐大且需處理迫切的健康問題而分身乏術，這使得他們難以針對戒菸或減重等生活型態的改變提供建議。專家警告，這阻礙了醫療體系在疾病發生前進行預防的目標。英國皇家全科醫師學院主張，政府必須聘僱更多醫師才能解決此問題。

paragraphs.en: For many years, a friendly conversation with a family doctor—known as a GP in the UK—was a normal part of visiting a medical clinic. Patients could talk about their lives, their stress, and their general health. However, a new report suggests that this important part of healthcare is disappearing. According to The Guardian Health, three out of four GPs now feel they are too busy to have deep, meaningful conversations with the people they treat.
paragraphs.zh: 多年來，與家庭醫師（在英國稱為全科醫師）進行友好的交談，是前往醫療診所看診時的日常。病患可以談論他們的生活、壓力以及整體健康狀況。然而，一份新的報告指出，醫療保健中這項重要的環節正在消失。根據《衛報健康版》（The Guardian Health）報導，四分之三的全科醫師現在覺得自己太過忙碌，無法與治療的對象進行深入且有意義的對話。

paragraphs.en: This problem is largely caused by the high number of patients that doctors must see every day. Most appointments are limited to only 10 minutes. In such a short time, doctors must focus on the most urgent health issues, such as new symptoms or immediate pain. As a result, there is very little time left to talk about long-term health goals, such as how to stop smoking, how to lose weight, or how to get better sleep. These conversations are important because they help patients stay healthy and avoid serious illnesses in the future.
paragraphs.zh: 這個問題主要是由醫師每天必須看診的龐大病患數量所導致。大多數的預約時間僅限於十分鐘。在如此短暫的時間內，醫師必須專注於最迫切的健康問題，例如新出現的症狀或立即性的疼痛。結果，幾乎沒有時間討論長期的健康目標，例如如何戒菸、如何減重，或是如何改善睡眠。這些對話非常重要，因為它們能幫助病患保持健康，並在未來避免嚴重的疾病。

paragraphs.en: Prof Victoria Tzortziou Brown, the president of the Royal College of GPs, explained that doctors always try to help with the main problem a patient brings to the office. However, she noted that it is difficult to look at a patient’s health in a 'holistic' way—meaning looking at the whole person rather than just one specific illness—when the waiting room is full. She said that while a doctor might quickly tell a patient to stop smoking, they often do not have the time to discuss why the patient finds it difficult to quit or what kind of support would work best for them.
paragraphs.zh: 英國皇家全科醫師學院（Royal College of GPs）院長維多利亞·佐齊歐·布朗教授（Prof Victoria Tzortziou Brown）解釋說，醫師總是盡力協助病患提出的主要問題。然而她指出，當候診室擠滿人時，要以「全人」的角度——意即關注整個人而非僅針對單一疾病——來檢視病患的健康狀況相當困難。她表示，雖然醫師或許能快速建議病患戒菸，但通常沒有時間討論病患為何覺得難以戒除，或是哪種支持方式對他們最有效。

paragraphs.en: This situation is causing concern among health experts. The King’s Fund, a group that studies the healthcare system, described the findings as 'alarming.' Sarah Woolnough, the chief executive of the organization, noted that the UK has a lower life expectancy than many similar countries. She warned that when doctors are too overwhelmed to provide preventative care—which means medical actions taken to stop a disease before it happens—they may miss early signs of health conditions that could have been treated more easily if caught sooner.
paragraphs.zh: 這種情況引起了健康專家的擔憂。研究醫療保健系統的組織「國王基金會」（The King’s Fund）將這些發現描述為「令人震驚」。該組織執行長莎拉·伍爾諾（Sarah Woolnough）指出，英國的平均餘命低於許多類似國家。她警告，當醫師忙到無法提供預防性照護——意即在疾病發生前採取醫療行動——他們可能會錯過健康狀況的早期徵兆，而這些狀況若能及早發現，原本可以更容易治療。

paragraphs.en: These findings create a difficult challenge for the government. Last year, officials announced a 10-year health plan that aims to move the National Health Service (NHS) 'from sickness to prevention.' The goal is to focus more on keeping people healthy so they do not need to go to the hospital as often. However, many experts now argue that this goal is impossible to reach under the current conditions. As Sarah Woolnough stated, talk about preventing sickness is meaningless if doctors cannot even find the time to cover the basics of healthy living during a regular visit.
paragraphs.zh: 這些發現為政府帶來了艱鉅的挑戰。去年，官員宣布了一項十年健康計畫，旨在將國家醫療保健服務（NHS）從「治療疾病」轉向「預防疾病」。目標是更專注於維持民眾健康，讓他們不必頻繁前往醫院。然而，許多專家現在主張，在目前的條件下，這個目標是不可能實現的。正如莎拉·伍爾諾所言，如果醫師在常規看診時連討論健康生活基本原則的時間都沒有，那麼談論預防疾病就毫無意義。

paragraphs.en: Many GPs feel frustrated by this situation. They were trained to provide comprehensive care that addresses both the physical and mental well-being of their patients. Now, they feel that the system forces them to act more like machines that process people as quickly as possible, rather than partners in their patients' long-term health. The Royal College of GPs has stated clearly that the only way to fix this is to employ more doctors. They believe that increasing the number of staff is the only way to ensure that GPs have enough time to listen, advise, and support their patients properly.
paragraphs.zh: 許多全科醫師對這種情況感到挫折。他們受過專業訓練，旨在提供兼顧病患身心健康的全面性照護。現在，他們覺得體制迫使他們表現得更像處理病患的機器，而非病患長期健康的夥伴。英國皇家全科醫師學院已明確表示，解決此問題的唯一方法就是聘僱更多醫師。他們認為，增加人力是確保全科醫師有足夠時間傾聽、建議並妥善支持病患的唯一途徑。

paragraphs.en: Ultimately, the debate highlights a major gap between the government's future plans for the health service and the daily reality inside local clinics. While the intention to focus on prevention is widely supported by health professionals, the current pressure on family doctors makes it very hard to turn that vision into reality. Without more time and more staff, the dream of a healthcare system that focuses on staying well, rather than just treating the sick, will remain difficult to achieve. For now, patients and doctors alike are waiting to see if the government will take the necessary steps to provide the support that the system desperately needs.
paragraphs.zh: 歸根究柢，這場辯論凸顯了政府對醫療服務的未來規劃與地方診所內的日常現實之間存在巨大落差。儘管專注於預防的意圖受到醫療專業人員的廣泛支持，但家庭醫師目前面臨的壓力，使得將該願景轉化為現實變得非常困難。若沒有更多的時間與人力，一個專注於維持健康而非僅是治療病患的醫療體系夢想，將難以實現。目前，病患與醫師都在等待，看政府是否會採取必要措施，提供該體系迫切需要的支持。

sources.title: Three in four UK GPs ‘too busy to talk to their patients in depth’

quiz.question: According to the article, why are GPs currently unable to discuss long-term health goals with their patients?

options.A: They lack the necessary training to provide advice on lifestyle changes.
options.B: The 10-minute appointment limit forces them to prioritize immediate symptoms.
options.C: Patients are no longer interested in talking about their general well-being.
options.D: The government has banned doctors from discussing topics like smoking or weight loss.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 B。根據文章第二段，由於門診時間限制在 10 分鐘內，醫生必須專注於處理急迫的健康問題（如新症狀或疼痛），因此沒有時間討論長期健康目標。選項 A 錯誤，因為醫生受過相關訓練。選項 C 錯誤，文中並未提及病患失去興趣。選項 D 錯誤，政府並未禁止此類討論，而是體制壓力導致無法執行。

quiz.question: What can be inferred about the government's 10-year health plan?

options.A: It is already showing success in reducing hospital visits.
options.B: It focuses primarily on increasing the salaries of family doctors.
options.C: Its success is hindered by a contradiction between policy goals and clinical reality.
options.D: It was designed by the Royal College of GPs to improve patient-doctor relationships.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 C。文章第五段與第七段提到，政府目標是將醫療體系轉向「預防」，但專家認為在現有醫師過勞、缺乏人力與時間的條件下，這個目標幾乎不可能實現。選項 A 錯誤，文中指出該目標難以達成。選項 B 錯誤，文中未提到加薪。選項 D 錯誤，計畫是由政府宣布的，而非該協會設計。

quiz.question: In the fourth paragraph, what does the word 'alarming' mean in the context of the King’s Fund's reaction?
quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 B。在文中，King’s Fund 用 'alarming' 來形容 GP 無法提供預防性照護的現況，這暗示了情況嚴重且令人擔憂，需要被重視。選項 A 的「困惑」語氣太輕；選項 C 的「憤怒」在文中並未體現；選項 D 的「安靜」與該詞的負面警示意義完全相反。

quiz.question: What is the central message of the article?

options.A: GPs are choosing to spend less time with patients to increase their own profits.
options.B: The UK healthcare system is failing because patients are not taking responsibility for their health.
options.C: Modern medicine has become too complicated for family doctors to manage alone.
options.D: Workload pressures on GPs are preventing them from providing the holistic, preventative care that the health system needs.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 D。全文的核心在於探討 GP 因門診壓力過大，無法進行深度對談與預防性醫療，這與政府推動的「預防勝於治療」願景產生嚴重落差。選項 A 錯誤，文中強調的是體制壓力而非醫生主觀意願。選項 B 錯誤，重點在於體制而非病患責任。選項 C 錯誤，文中並未說醫療太複雜，而是時間太少。
